questions.q: Let $f(x)=\int x^3 \sqrt{3-x^2} d x$. If $5 f(\sqrt{2})=-4$, then $f(1)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Let } 3-x^2=t^2 \\ & +x d x=-t d t \\ & f(x)=\int\left(3-t^2\right) \cdot t(-t d t)+c \\ & =\int\left(\mathrm{t}^4-3 \mathrm{t}^2\right) \mathrm{dt}+\mathrm{c} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{t}^5}{5}-\mathrm{t}^3+\mathrm{c} \\ & \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{\left(3-\mathrm{x}^2\right)^{5 / 2}}{5}-\left(3-\mathrm{x}^2\right)^{3 / 2}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \mathrm{f}(\sqrt{2})=\frac{1}{5}-1+\mathrm{c}=-\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{c}=0 \\ & \mathrm{f}(1)=\frac{2^{5 / 2}}{5}-2^{3 / 2} \\ & =2^{1 / 2}\left(\frac{4}{5}-2\right) \\ & \mathrm{f}(1)-\frac{-6 \sqrt{2}}{5}\end{aligned}$

Let

$I = {∫}_{0}^{∞}\left(\dfrac{6}{e^{3x} + 6e^{2x} + 11e^{x} + 6}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{6}{\left(e^{x} + 1\right)\left(e^{x} + 2\right)\left(e^{x} + 3\right)}dx$

Using partial fraction, we can write

$⇒ I = 6{∫}_{0}^{∞}\left[\dfrac{1}{2\left(e^{x} + 1\right)} - 1\left(e^{x} + 2\right) + \dfrac{1}{2\left(e^{x} + 3\right)}\right]dx$

$⇒ I = 6{∫}_{0}^{∞}\left[\dfrac{1}{2\left(e^{- x} + 1\right)} - 1\left(1 + 2e^{- x}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2\left(1 + 3e^{- x}\right)}\right]e^{- x}dx$

$⇒ I = 6{- \dfrac{1}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(e^{- x} + 1\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(2e^{- x} + 1\right) - \dfrac{1}{6}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(3e^{- x} + 1\right)}_{0}^{∞}$

$⇒ I = 6 \left[0 - \left$\{- $\dfrac{1}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}$2 + $\dfrac{1}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}$3 - $\dfrac{1}{6}\log_{\mathrm{e}}$4\right\}\right]$

$⇒ I = 3\log_{\mathrm{e}}2 - 3\log_{\mathrm{e}}3 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}4$

$⇒ I = 5\log_{\mathrm{e}}2 - 3\log_{\mathrm{e}}3$

$⇒ I = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{32}{27}\right)$

$

questions.q: $∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{5x}{2}}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$, is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{5x}{2}}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{sin\left(2x + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$

Using~$sin\left(A + B\right) = sinAcosB + cosAsinB$

$= ∫ \dfrac{sin2xcos\dfrac{x}{2} + cos2xsin\dfrac{x}{2}}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$

$= ∫ \left(\dfrac{\left(2sinxcosx\right)cos\dfrac{x}{2}}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}} + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(\dfrac{2\left(2sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right)cosxcos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}} + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(4\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)cosx + cos2x\right)dx$

Using $cos2x = 2\cos^{2}x - 1 ⇒ 2\cos^{2}x = 1 + cos2x$

$= ∫ \left(2\left(1 + cosx\right)cosx + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(2cosx + 2\cos^{2}x + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(2cosx + \left(1 + cos2x\right) + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(2cosx + 2cos2x + 1\right)dx$

$= 2sinx + sin2x + x + c$, where~$c$& is the constant of integration.

questions.q: If& $∫ \left(e^{2x} + 2e^{x} - e^{- x} - 1\right)e\left(e^{x} + e^{- x}\right)dx = g ( x ) e\left(e^{x} + e^{- x}\right) + c,$ where~$c$ is a constant of integration, then~$g ( 0 )$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \left(e^{2x} + 2e^{x} - e^{- x} - 1\right)e\left(e^{x} + e^{- x}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \left(e^{2x} + e^{x} - 1\right)e\left(e^{x} + e^{- x}\right)dx + ∫ \left(e^{x} - e^{- x}\right)e^{e^{x} + e^{- x}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \left(e^{x} + 1 - e^{- x}\right)e^{e^{x} + e^{- x} + x}dx + e^{e^{x} + e^{- x}} + c$

$e^{x} + e^{- x} + x = u$

\left(e^{x} - e^{- x} + 1\right)dx = du$

$I = e^{e^{x} + e^{- x} + x} + e^{e^{x} + e^{- x}} + c = e^{e^{x} + e^{- x}}\left(e^{x} + 1\right) + c$

then $g ( x ) = e^{x} + 1$

$g ( 0 ) = 2$

$

questions.q: Let $\int \frac{2-\tan x}{3+\tan x} \mathrm{~d} x=\frac{1}{2}\left(\alpha x+\log _{\mathrm{e}}|\beta \sin x+\gamma \cos x|\right)+C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration. Then $\alpha+\frac{\gamma}{\beta}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{2-\tan x}{3+\tan x} d x=\int \frac{2 \cos x-\sin x}{3 \cos x+\sin x} d x \\ & 2 \cos x-\sin x=A(3 \cos x+\sin x)+B(\cos x-3 \sin x) \\ & 3 A+B=2 \\ & A-3 B=-1\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{2}, B=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \therefore \int \frac{2 \cos x-\sin x}{3 \cos x+\sin x} d x \\ & =\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \ln |3 \cos x+\sin x|+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2}(x+\ln |3 \cos x+\sin x|)+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2}(\alpha x+\ln |\beta \sin x+\gamma \cos x|)+C \\ & \alpha=1, \beta=1, \gamma=3 \\ & \therefore \alpha+\frac{\gamma}{\beta}=1+\frac{3}{1}=4\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of the integral& $∫ \dfrac{sin\theta \cdot sin2\theta\left(\sin^{6}\theta + \sin^{4}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta\right)\sqrt{2\sin^{4}\theta + 3\sin^{2}\theta + 6}}{1 - cos2\theta}d\theta$ is (where $c$ is a constant of integration)

questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\theta \cdot sin2\theta\left(\sin^{6}\theta + \sin^{4}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta\right)\sqrt{2\sin^{4}\theta + 3\sin^{2}\theta + 6}}{1 - cos2\theta}d\theta$

$= ∫ \sin^{2}\theta \cdot cos\theta\left(\sin^{4}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta + 1\right)\left(2\sin^{4}\theta + 3\sin^{2}\theta + 6\right)1 / 2d\theta$

Let $sin\theta = t ⇒ cos\thetad\theta = dt$

$= ∫ \left(t^{5} + t^{3} + t\right)t\left(2t^{4} + 3t^{2} + 6\right)1 / 2dt$

$= ∫ \left(t^{5} + t^{3} + t\right)\left(t^{2}\right)1 / 2\left(2t^{4} + 3t^{2} + 6\right)1 / 2dt$

$= ∫ \left(t^{5} + t^{3} + t\right)\left(2t^{6} + 3t^{4} + 6t^{2}\right)1 / 2dt$

Let~$2t^{6} + 3t^{4} + 6t^{2} = u^{2}$

$∴ I = ∫ \left(u^{2}\right)1 / 2 \cdot \dfrac{2udu}{12}$

$= ∫ \dfrac{u2}{6}du = \dfrac{u3}{18} + C$

$= \dfrac{\left(2t^{6} + 3t^{4} + 6t^{2}\right)3 / 2}{18} + C$

when $t = sin\theta$

questions.q: If $∫ e^{secx}\left(secxtanxf\left(x\right) + \left(secxtanx + sec^{2}x\right)\right)dx = e^{secx}f  \left(x\right) + C,$~then a possible choice of $f\left(x\right) is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$∫ e^{sec ⁡ x} ( sec ⁡ xtan ⁡ xf\left(x\right) + \left(sec ⁡ xtan ⁡ x + \sec^{2} ⁡ x\right)dx = e^{sec ⁡ x}f\left(x\right) + C$

Differentiating~both sides w.r.t $‘x’$~we get

$e^{secx}\left(secxtanxf\left(x\right) + \left(secxtanx + \sec^{2}x\right)\right) = \left(e^{secx} ⋅ secxtanx\right)f ( x ) + e^{secx}f^{'}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \sec^{2}x + tanxsecx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \left(\sec^{2}x + tanxsecx\right)dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = tanx + secx + c, c \in R$
Hence, possible choice is $f\left(x\right) = secx + tanx + \dfrac{1}{2} .$

$

questions.q: Let $f \left(x\right) = ∫ $\dfrac{2x}{ \left(x^{2} + 1\right) \left(x^{2} + 3\right)}$dx$.~If $f \left(3\right) = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$5 - \log_{\mathrm{e}}6\right)$, then $f  \left(4\right)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$I = ∫ \dfrac{2x}{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)\left(x^{2} + 3\right)}dx$

Put~$x^{2} = t ⇒ 2xdx = dt$

$I = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(t + 1\right)\left(t + 3\right)}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{2}{\left(t + 1\right)\left(t + 3\right)}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{t + 1} - \dfrac{1}{t + 3}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln\left(t + 1\right) - ln\left(t + 3\right)\right] + C$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln\left(x^{2} + 1\right) - ln\left(x^{2} + 3\right)\right] + C$

Put~$x = 3$, then

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln5 - ln6\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln10 - ln12\right] + C$

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln5 - ln6\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln2 + ln5 - ln2 - ln6\right] + C$

$⇒ C = 0$

So,

$f \left(x\right) = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left[$ln \left(x^{2} + 1\right) - ln\left(x^{2} + 3\right)\right]$

$⇒ f \left(4\right) = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left(ln17 - ln19\right)$~or~$f \left($4\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}17 - \log_{\mathrm{e}}19\right)$

$

questions.q: Let $I(x)=\int \frac{6}{\sin ^2 x(1-\cot x)^2} d x$. If $I(0)=3$, then $I  \left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right)is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$I(x)=\int \frac{6 d x}{\sin ^2 x(1-\cot x)^2}=\int \frac{6 \operatorname{cosec}^2 x d x}{(1-\cot x)^2}$
Put $1-\cot x=t\operatorname{cosec}^2 \mathrm{xdx}=\mathrm{dt}\begin{aligned} & I=\int \frac{6 d t}{t^2}=\frac{-6}{t}+c \\ & I(x)=\frac{-6}{1-\cot x} c, c=3 \\ & I(x)=3-\frac{6}{1-\cot x}, I\left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right)=3-\frac{6}{1-(2+\sqrt{3})} \\ & I\left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right)=3+\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}+1}=3+\frac{6(\sqrt{3}-1)}{2}=3 \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The integral& $∫ \left(\dfrac{x}{xsinx + cosx}\right)2dx$ is equal to, (where~$C$ is a constant of integration):
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$∫ \dfrac{x^{2}dx}{\left(xsinx + cosx\right)2} = ∫ \dfrac{x}{cosx} ⋅ \dfrac{xcosx}{\left(xsinx + cosx\right)2}dx$

$= \dfrac{x}{cosx} ∫ \dfrac{xcosx}{\left(xsinx + cosx\right)2}dx - ∫ \left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(xsecx\right) ∫ \dfrac{xcosx}{\left(xsinx + cosx\right)2}dx\right]dx$

$= \dfrac{x}{cosx}\left(- \dfrac{1}{xsinx + cosx}\right) + ∫ \sec^{2}xdx$,~$\text{∵} ∫ \dfrac{xcosx}{\left(xsinx + cosx\right)2}dx = \dfrac{- 1}{xsinx + cosx}$

$ \text{ and } \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(xsecx\right) = secx + xsecxtanx = secx \left(1 + $\dfrac{xsinx}{cosx}\right) = {\sec^{2}x\left($xsinx + cosx\right)$

$= \dfrac{- x}{cosx\left(xsinx + cosx\right)} + \dfrac{sinx}{cosx} +C$

$= tanx - \dfrac{xsecx}{xsinx + cosx} +C$

$

The integral $∫ \dfrac{e^{3\log_{\mathrm{e}}2x} + 5e^{2\log_{\mathrm{e}}2x}}{e^{4\log_{\mathrm{e}}x} + 5e^{3\log_{\mathrm{e}}x} - 7e^{2\log_{\mathrm{e}}x}}dx, x > 0$, is equal to

questions.solution:
$∫ \dfrac{e^{3\log_{\mathrm{e}}2x} + 5e^{2\log_{\mathrm{e}}2x}}{e^{4\log_{\mathrm{e}}x} + 5e^{3\log_{\mathrm{e}}x} - 7e^{2\log_{\mathrm{e}}x}}dx, x > 0$

$= ∫ \dfrac{\left(2x\right)3 + 5\left(2x\right)2}{x^{4} + 5x^{3} - 7x^{2}}dx = ∫ \dfrac{4x^{2}\left(2x + 5\right)}{x^{2}\left(x^{2} + 5x - 7\right)}dx$

questions.q: $∫ \dfrac{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)e^{x}}{\left(x + 1\right)2}dx = f\left(x\right)e^{x} + C$, where~$C$~is a~constant, then $\dfrac{d^{3}f}{dx^{3}}$~at $x = 1$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
& $∫ \dfrac{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)e^{x}dx}{\left(x + 1\right)2} = f\left(x\right)e^{x} + C$

$∫ e^{x}\left(\dfrac{x^{2} - 1}{\left(x + 1\right)2} + \dfrac{2}{\left(x + 1\right)2}\right)dx = f\left(x\right)e^{x} + C$

$∫ e^{x}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1} + \dfrac{2}{\left(x + 1\right)2}\right)dx = f\left(x\right)e^{x} + C$

We know that~$∫ e^{x}\left(f\left(x\right) + f^{'}\left(x\right)\right) = e^{x}f\left(x\right) + c$

Here~$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1} \text{ and } f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{\left(x + 1\right)2}$

So~$∫ e^{x}\left(\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right) + \dfrac{2}{( x + 1{)}^{2}}\right)dx = f\left(x\right)e^{x} + C$

$⇒ e^{x}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right) + C = e^{x}f\left(x\right) + C$

On comparing both sides we get~$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}$

So~$f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{\left(x + 1\right)2} \text{ and } f^{"}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 4}{\left(x + 1\right)3}$

$f^{'''}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{12}{\left(x + 1\right)4}$~,

Now~$f^{'''}\left(1\right) = \dfrac{12}{\left(1 + 1\right)4} = \dfrac{12}{16} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: For $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta \in \mathbb{N}$, if $∫ \left(\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)2x + \left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)2x\right)\log_{\mathrm{e}}xdx = \dfrac{1}{α}\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)\betax - \dfrac{1}{γ}\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)\deltax + C$, where $e = \mathop{∑}_{n = 0}^{∞}\dfrac{1}{n !}$ and $C$ is constant of integration, then $\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 4\delta$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \left(\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)2x + \left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)2x\right)lnxdx = \dfrac{1}{α}\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)\betax - \dfrac{1}{γ}\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)\deltax + C$

Now let~$I = ∫ \left(\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)2x + \left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)2x\right)lnxdx$

Now let~\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)2x = t$

$⇒ 2x\left(lnx - 1\right) = lnt$

$⇒ lnxdx = \dfrac{1}{2t}dt$

So,~$I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)\dfrac{dt}{t}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{t2}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right) + c$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)2x - \left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)2x\right) + C$

Now on comparing with~$I = \dfrac{1}{α}\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)\betax - \dfrac{1}{γ}\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)\deltax + C$, we get~$\alpha = 2, \beta = 2, \gamma = 2, \delta = 2$

Hence,~$\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 4\delta = 2 + 4 + 6 - 8 = 4$

Hence this is the required option. \text{ and }

$

questions.q: If $∫ x^{5}e^{- x^{2}}dx = g  \left(x\right)e^{- x^{2}} + c$,~where $c$ is a constant of integration, then $g\left(-1\right) is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $I = ∫ x^{5}e^{- x^{2}}dx$

Let,~$- x^{2} = t ⇒ xdx = - \dfrac{1}{2}dt$

$∴ I = - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ t^{2}e^{t}dt$

By using integrating by parts, i.e.~$∫ \left(u \cdot v\right)dx = u ∫ vdx - ∫ \left[\dfrac{d}{dx}u ∫ vdx\right]dx + c,$~we get

$I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[t^{2} ∫ e^{t}dt - ∫ \left(2t ∫ e^{t}dt\right)dt\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[t^{2}e^{t} - 2 ∫ te^{t}dt\right] + c$

Again, applying~integrating by parts, we get

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[t^{2}e^{t} - 2\left(t ∫ e^{t}dt - ∫ 1 \cdot e^{t}dt\right)\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[t^{2}e^{t} - 2\left(te^{t} - e^{t}\right)\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[t^{2}e^{t} - 2te^{t} + 2e^{t}\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{et}{2}\left[t^{2} - 2t + 2\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{e- x^{2}}{2}\left[x^{4} + 2x^{2} + 2\right] + c$

Given,~$I = ∫ x^{5}e^{- x^{2}}dx = g \left(x\right)e^{- x^{2}} + c$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = - $\dfrac{1}{2}\left($x^{4} + 2x^{2} + 2\right)$

$⇒ g \left(-1\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\left(-$1\right)4 + 2\left(-1\right)2 + 2\right)$

$⇒ g\left(-1\right) = - $\dfrac{5}{2} .

$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x^{4}} d x=A(\mathrm{x})\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)^{m}+C,$ for a suitable chosen integer $\mathrm{m}$ and a function $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{x})$, where $\mathrm{C}$ is a constant of integration, then $(\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{x}))^{\mathrm{m}}$ equals :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$A(x)\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)^{m}+C=\int \frac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x^{4}} d x=\int \frac{\sqrt{\frac{1}{x^{2}}-1}}{x^{3}} d x$ Let $\frac{1}{x^{2}}-1=u^{2}\$Rightarrow-\frac{2}{x^{3}}=\frac{2 u d u}{d x}\frac{d x}{x^{3}}=-$u d $uA(x)\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\rright)^{m}+C=\int\left(-u^{2}\right) d u=-\frac{u^{3}}{3}+C
=-\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}-1\$right)^{\frac{3}{2}}+C
$=-\frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{x^{3}} \cdot\left($1-x^{2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}$+C
$=\frac{-1}{3 x^{3}}\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)^{3}+$C
Compare both sides,
\Rightarrow $A(x)=-\frac{1}{3 x^{3}}$and m=3
\Rightarrow(A(x))^{3}=\frac{-1}{27 x^{9}}

questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{1}{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}}dx = g  \left($x\right) + c, g \left(1\right) = 0$, then $g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \dfrac{1}{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}}dx = g\left(x\right) + c$

Put $x = cos2\theta$

$dx = - 2sin2\theta \cdot d\theta$

$= ∫ \dfrac{1}{cos2\theta}tan\theta\left(- 4sin\theta \cdot cos\theta\right)d\theta$

$= ∫ \dfrac{1}{cos2\theta}\left(- 4\sin^{2}\theta\right)d\theta$

$= - 2 ∫ \dfrac{1 - cos2\theta}{cos2\theta}d\theta$

$= - \dfrac{2}{2}ln\left|sec2\theta - tan2\theta\right| + 2\theta + c$

$= ln\left|sec2\theta - tan2\theta\right| + 2\theta + c$

$= ln\left|\dfrac{1 - sin2\theta}{cos2\theta}\right| + \cos^{- 1}x + c$

$\mathop{= ln\left|\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}{x}\right| + \cos^{- 1}x + c ⏟}_{g\left(x\right)}$

$∴ g\left(1\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 0$

So,~$g\left(x\right) = ln\left|\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}{x}\right| + \cos^{- 1}x$

$g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = ln\left|2 - \sqrt{3}\right| + \dfrac{π}{3}$

$g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = ln\left|\dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1}\right| + \dfrac{π}{3}$

questions.q: & If $∫ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x}{1 + x}\right)dx = A\left(x\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right) + B\left(x\right) + C$, where~$C$~is a constant of integration, then the ordered~pair  \left(A \left(x\right), B \left($x\right)\right) can be :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x}{1 + x}\right)dx$

$= ∫ \mathop{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right) ⏟}_{I}\mathop{\left(1\right) ⏟}_{II}dx$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - ∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + x} . \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} . xdx + C$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{t . 2t . dt}{1 + t^{2}} + C$~$($putting~$x = t^{2} ⇒ dx = 2tdt )$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - ∫ \dfrac{t2}{1 + t^{2}}dt + C$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - t + \tan^{- 1}t + C$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x} + \tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} + C$

$= \left(x + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x} + C$

Comparing with~$A\left(x\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right) + B\left(x\right) + C$, we get

\left(A \left(x\right), B \left(x\right)\right) = \left(x + 1, - \sqrt{x}\right)$

$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{2 x^2+5 x+9}{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}} \mathrm{~d} x=x \sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\alpha \sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\beta \log _e\left|x+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{x^2+x+1}\right|+\mathrm{C}$, where $C$ is the constant of integration, then $\alpha+2 \beta$ is equal to $\qquad$ _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 2 \mathrm{x}^2+5 \mathrm{x}+9=\mathrm{A}\left(\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1\right)+\mathrm{B}(2 \mathrm{x}+1)+\mathrm{C} \\ & \mathrm{A}=2 \quad \mathrm{~B}=\frac{3}{2} \quad \mathrm{C}=\frac{11}{2} \\ & 2 \int \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1} \mathrm{dx}+\frac{3}{2} \int \frac{2 \mathrm{x}+1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}} \mathrm{dx}+\frac{11}{2} \int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}} \\ & 2 \int \sqrt{\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2} \mathrm{dx}+3 \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}+\frac{11}{2} \int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\sqrt{\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}} \\ & 2\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}}{2} \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}+\frac{3}{8} \ln \left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}\right)\right)+3 \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1} \\ & +\frac{11}{2} \ell \mathrm{n}\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}\right)+\mathrm{C} \\ & \alpha=\frac{7}{2} \quad\beta=\frac{25}{4} \\& \alpha+2 \beta=16 \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If $\int \operatorname{cosec}^5 x d x=\alpha \cot x \operatorname{cosec} x\left(\operatorname{cossc}^2 x+\frac{3}{2}\right)+\beta \log _\epsilon\left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right|+C$
where $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ is the constant of integration, then the value of $8(\alpha+\beta)$ equals _______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x \cdot \operatorname{cosec}^2 x d x=I$
By applying integration by parts $\begin{aligned} & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x+\int \cot x\left(-3 \operatorname{cosec}^2 x \cot x \operatorname{cosec} x\right) d x \\ & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-3 \int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x-1\right) d x \\ & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-3 I+3 \int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x d x \end{aligned}$ let $\begin{aligned} & I_1=\int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x d x=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x-\int \cot ^2 x \operatorname{cosec} x d x \\ & I_1=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x-\int\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x-1\right) \operatorname{cosec} x d x \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & 2 I_1=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right| \\ & I_1=-\frac{1}{2} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right| \\ & 4 I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-\frac{3}{2} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\frac{3}{2} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right|+4 c \\ & I=-\frac{1}{4} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x+\frac{3}{2}\right)+\frac{3}{8} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right|+c \\ & \therefore \alpha=\frac{-1}{4}, \beta=\frac{3}{8} \rightarrow 8(\alpha+\beta)=1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\begin{aligned} \int\left(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^3}\right) & \left(\sqrt[23]{3 x^{-24}+x^{-26}}\right) d x \\ & =-\frac{\alpha}{3(\alpha+1)}\left(3 x^\beta+x^\gamma\right)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{\alpha}}+C, x \gt 0,\end{aligned}(\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in Z)$, where $C$ is the constant of integration, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to ________ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^4}\right)\left(\frac{3}{\mathrm{x}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)^{\frac{1}{23}} \mathrm{dx} \\ & \text { using } \mathrm{t}=\frac{3}{\mathrm{x}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3} \Rightarrow \mathrm{dt}=-3\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^4}\right) \mathrm{dx} \\ & \int \frac{\mathrmt^{1 / 23} \mathrm{dt}}{-3}=\frac{\mathrmt^{24 / 23}}{\left(\frac{24}{23}\right)(-3)}+C \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=23 \beta=-1 \gamma=-3 \\ & \alpha+\beta+\gamma=19\end{aligned}$
